look_here_first: LOOK HERE FIRST · American black nightshade is an UNARMED, green herb with simple alternate ovate leaves and VERY SMALL white five-lobed star flowers, often in compact clusters. On mature plants, inspect the SMALL (~5–10 mm) SHINY PURPLE-BLACK BERRIES and the tiny green CALYX LOBES bent sharply BACK from the base of each ripe berry. Check SHORT, plump yellow anthers (~0.7–1.5 mm) with a hand lens or macro photo. Crucially: multiple black nightshade species look like this from a distance—green fruit or white petals alone cannot prove S. americanum.

key_traits.label: Field character
key_traits.text: unarmed green annual to short-lived perennial, erect to spreading up to about 1.5 m

key_traits.label: Field character
key_traits.text: ALTERNATE simple ovate/elliptic leaves, typically 2–10.5 × 1–4.5 cm, smooth to slightly wavy or shallowly toothed

key_traits.label: Field character
key_traits.text: usually 3–10 tiny white flowers borne together on simple, often umbrella-like stalk groups

key_traits.label: Field character
key_traits.text: white five-lobed corolla, typically only 4–8 mm across (occasional larger variation)

key_traits.label: Field character
key_traits.text: five SHORT yellow anthers, about 0.7–1.5 mm long

key_traits.label: Field character
key_traits.text: green pea-size developing berries turning GLOSSY purple-black, approximately 5–10 mm wide

key_traits.label: Field character
key_traits.text: mature fruit calyx lobes tiny and STRONGLY REFLEXED (pointing backwards away from berry)

key_traits.label: Field character
key_traits.text: mature berry pedicels often ERECT or SPREADING, with the berry separating and leaving its stalk attached to plant

lookalikes.differences: The hardest look-alikes are OTHER unarmed black-berried Solanum species, particularly S. emulans and S. nigrescens, not the large prickly yellow-fruited species. Distinguish with anther length, fruit gloss, reflexed versus appressed fruit calyx, and pedicel behavior.
